questions.q: What is the range of integers that can be represented in 8-bit two's complement form?
questions.exp: n-bit two's complement range is -2^(n-1) to 2^(n-1) - 1, i.e. -128 to +127.

questions.q: Which of the following is a lossless image compression format?
questions.exp: PNG uses lossless DEFLATE compression; JPEG, MP3 and MPEG are lossy.

questions.q: For a half subtractor computing A - B, the Borrow output is
questions.exp: A borrow is needed only when A = 0 and B = 1, so Borrow = A'B.

questions.q: The kernels of Windows NT and macOS are best described as:
options: hybrid kernels (microkernel ideas with monolithic components)
questions.exp: Hybrid kernels combine a microkernel-style design with some services kept in kernel space for speed. Windows NT and macOS (XNU) are standard examples; Linux is monolithic with loadable modules.

questions.q: Tables A(id) = {1,2,3} and B(id) = {2,3,4}. How many rows does SELECT * FROM A FULL OUTER JOIN B ON A.id = B.id return?
questions.exp: Matches: 2 and 3 (2 rows). Unmatched A row 1 and unmatched B row 4 add 2 more rows: 4 in total.

questions.q: The solution of T(n) = 4T(n/2) + n² is
questions.exp: a=4, b=2, n^(log₂4) = n² matches f(n) = n², case 2 gives Θ(n² log n).

questions.q: The cache is accessed first (10 ns) and, on a miss, main memory is then accessed (additional 100 ns). With a hit ratio of 0.9, the average memory access time is
questions.exp: AMAT = hit time + miss rate × miss penalty = 10 + 0.1 × 100 = 20 ns.

questions.q: A microcontroller differs from a microprocessor mainly because a microcontroller integrates on one chip
options: CPU along with RAM, ROM, timers and I/O ports
questions.exp: A microcontroller is a computer on a chip: CPU plus memory and peripherals, whereas a microprocessor is essentially only the CPU.

questions.q: In an RSA system p = 3, q = 11 and e = 7. The ciphertext for plaintext m = 2 is
BFS is run on a connected undirected graph. The graph is bipartite if and only if
options: no edge joins two vertices at the same BFS level
no edge joins vertices in consecutive levels
questions.exp: Colour vertices by level parity; an edge inside one level would close an odd cycle.

questions.q: The race-around condition in a JK flip-flop (J = K = 1) is eliminated by
options: increasing the width of the clock pulse
questions.exp: A master-slave arrangement lets the output change only after the clock goes low, so output cannot toggle repeatedly in one clock pulse.

questions.q: Which string method raises a ValueError when the substring is not found?
questions.exp: find() returns -1 whereas index() raises ValueError.

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-functional requirement?
options: The system shall calculate income tax from the salary entered
The system shall allow users to search products by name
The system shall respond to any search query within 2 seconds
The system shall generate a monthly sales report
questions.exp: Response time is a performance constraint (quality attribute), hence non-functional; the others describe functions.
__init__ stores v = 4 in the object; show prints self.v * 2 = 8.

questions.q: In the table-filling method for minimising a DFA, a pair of states (p, q) is marked in the first round when:
options: exactly one of p and q is a final state
both p and q are final states
both p and q are non-final states
questions.exp: A final and a non-final state are distinguished by the empty string; later rounds propagate marks.

questions.q: Which of the following sets of gates is NOT functionally complete?
questions.exp: Without an inversion capability, AND and OR alone cannot realise NOT, so the set is not complete.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of element comparisons binary search makes on a sorted array of 1000 elements (successful or unsuccessful)?
Which change alone does NOT allow two Java methods in the same class to be overloaded?
options: Changing the type of a parameter
Changing the order of parameters of different types
questions.exp: Overloading requires different parameter lists; a different return type alone causes a compile-time error.

questions.q: Which design pattern defines a one-to-many dependency so that when one object changes state all its dependents are notified automatically?
questions.exp: Observer is a behavioural pattern (publish-subscribe style). Singleton is creational; Adapter and Facade are structural.

questions.q: Which of the following is a link-state routing protocol?
questions.exp: OSPF floods link-state advertisements and runs Dijkstra's algorithm; RIP and IGRP are distance vector and BGP is path vector.
strlen excludes the terminating null (5) while sizeof counts it (6).

questions.q: What is the minimum number of moves required to solve the Tower of Hanoi puzzle with 5 disks?
questions.exp: Minimum moves = 2ⁿ - 1 = 2⁵ - 1 = 31.

questions.q: In the transaction state diagram, a transaction enters the 'partially committed' state
options: after its final statement has been executed
after the data is written to the log and the DB is closed
questions.exp: Active → partially committed occurs after the last statement executes; it becomes committed only after the changes are safely recorded.

questions.q: Which of the following is executed on the web server before the page is sent to the browser?
questions.exp: PHP is a server-side language; its output is sent to the client as HTML.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an application of a queue?
questions.exp: Postfix evaluation uses a stack; the others use FIFO queues.

questions.q: Evaluate the prefix expression: - * + 4 3 2 5
questions.exp: Scanning from the right: 4+3=7; 7*2=14; 14-5=9.

questions.q: Which of the following is a typical goal-driven (backward-chaining) application?
options: Firing alarms as sensor data keeps arriving
Adding every derivable fact from an order, as in XCON configuration
Generating all consequences of a new fact in a monitoring system
Diagnosing a suspected disease as in MYCIN or answering a Prolog query
questions.exp: Backward chaining starts from a hypothesis/goal and looks for rules and facts supporting it (MYCIN, Prolog).

questions.q: In an 8085 program, MVI A,45H is followed by ADI 3BH. What is the content of A and the Carry flag after ADI?
questions.exp: 45H + 3BH = 80H, which fits in 8 bits, so no carry is generated (CY = 0).

questions.q: In the SEI Capability Maturity Model (CMM), which maturity level is known as the 'Defined' level?
questions.exp: CMM levels are 1 Initial, 2 Repeatable, 3 Defined, 4 Managed, 5 Optimizing.

questions.q: What is the minimum number of relations (tables) needed to represent two entity sets E1 and E2 connected by a many-to-many relationship in the relational model?
questions.exp: One table per entity set plus a separate table for the M:N relationship holding both foreign keys: 3.

questions.q: A CPU has a 16-bit address bus. What is the maximum amount of memory it can directly address?
questions.exp: 2¹⁶ = 65536 locations = 64 KB (for byte addressing).

questions.q: Withdrawing money from an ATM using a debit card and a PIN is an example of
options: Two factors, both of the 'something you know' type
Two-factor authentication (something you have plus something you know)
questions.exp: The card is something you have and the PIN is something you know, so two different factor categories are used.

questions.q: A hash table with 10 slots uses chaining and h(k) = k mod 10. Keys 12, 22, 32, 15, 25 and 7 are inserted. What is the length of the longest chain?
questions.exp: 12, 22 and 32 all hash to slot 2 giving a chain of 3; slot 5 has 2 keys and slot 7 has 1.

questions.q: A C program calls fork() three times in sequence (no conditions). How many child processes are created in total?
questions.exp: Total processes = 2³ = 8, including the original, so 7 are children.

questions.q: Which of the following problems is decidable?
options: Whether a given Turing machine halts on a given input
Whether a given CFG is ambiguous
Whether two given CFGs generate the same language
Whether the language of a given DFA is empty
questions.exp: DFA emptiness is a reachability check on the state graph; the other problems are undecidable.

questions.q: What is the minimum size of an Ethernet frame (IEEE 802.3), including header and CRC?
questions.exp: Minimum Ethernet frame is 64 bytes (46 bytes minimum data plus 18 bytes of header and FCS).

questions.q: Which statement imports only the function ceil from the math module so that it can be called as ceil(2.1)?
questions.exp: The from ... import ... form brings the name directly into the current namespace.

questions.q: A 0/1 knapsack has capacity 7 and items (weight, value): (1,1), (3,4), (4,5), (5,7). The maximum total value is
questions.exp: Best feasible subsets: {3,4} gives 4+5 = 9; {1,5} gives 8; {5} gives 7. Maximum is 9.

questions.q: Which of the following lists the functions in increasing order of growth rate?
questions.exp: Polynomial functions grow slower than exponential, and n! grows faster than 2ⁿ.
The extraction operator >> reads whitespace-separated ints: a = 10, b = 20, so a + b = 30. The third value 30 is never read.

questions.q:
Statement I: csv.reader returns every row of a CSV file as a list of strings.
Statement II: csv.writer.writerows() accepts a single flat list and writes it as one row.
Which is correct?
options: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
Statement I is false and Statement II is true
questions.exp: writerows() expects an iterable of rows (e.g., a list of lists); writerow() writes a single row.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT true about UDP?
options: It provides in-order delivery of datagrams
It supports an optional checksum for error detection
questions.exp: UDP does not guarantee ordering or delivery; those are TCP features.

questions.q: In the checksum method with 1's-complement addition, the receiver finds no error when the 1's-complement sum of all words including the checksum is
options: equal to the first data word
questions.exp: The sender sends the complement of the sum, so the receiver's sum becomes all 1s (whose complement is 0) if there is no error.

questions.q: A malicious program that replicates itself and spreads across a network without needing a host file or user action is called a:
questions.exp: A worm is self-replicating and propagates on its own through the network. A virus needs a host file/user action, a Trojan hides inside a useful program, and a logic bomb triggers on a condition.

questions.q: Which type of firewall inspects the actual content of application-layer traffic such as HTTP or FTP and is generally the most secure but slowest?
questions.exp: Proxy/application gateways examine application data; packet filters only look at headers (IP, port, protocol).

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes a database schema from a database instance?
options: The schema is the data currently stored; the instance is the structure of the tables
The schema is the physical file layout; the instance is the set of views
Both terms mean the same thing; they differ only in the DBMS product
The schema is the logical structure (relations, attributes, domains) and changes rarely; the instance is the data stored at a given moment
questions.exp: Schema = design (like a class definition) and is stable; instance = snapshot of the tuples at a time (like the objects) and changes with every insert, delete or update.

questions.q: Which of the following grammars is ambiguous?
options: E → E+T | T ; T → T*F | F ; F → id
questions.exp: The string id+id*id has two distinct parse trees under E → E+E | E*E | id.
The macro expands textually to 2+3*2+3 = 2+6+3 = 11.

questions.q: For the grammar S → AB, A → a | ε, B → b, what is FIRST(S)?
questions.exp: FIRST(S) = FIRST(A) minus ε, plus FIRST(B) because A is nullable; B is not nullable so ε is excluded.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an unsupervised learning algorithm?
questions.exp: K-means groups unlabeled data into clusters; the others need labeled training data.

questions.q: For class Derived : public Base, when an object of Derived is created, the constructors run in the order:
options: Order is decided at run time
questions.exp: Base sub-objects are constructed first, then the derived part.

questions.q: In CSS, what does the selector p > span select?
options: All span elements inside any p at any depth
A span immediately following a p
Every span that is a direct child of a p
questions.exp: The child combinator '>' selects only direct children.

questions.q: Head at cylinder 50; request queue 82, 170, 43, 140, 24, 16, 190. What is the total head movement under SSTF?
In an expert system, which component is responsible for telling the user how or why a conclusion was reached?
questions.exp: The explanation facility justifies the reasoning steps and conclusions to the user.

questions.q: Which fopen() mode opens a file for both reading and writing and fails if the file does not exist?
questions.exp: "r+" requires an existing file and allows read and write; "w+" truncates/creates and "a+" creates if absent.

questions.q: Preemptive SJF (SRTF) with P1 (arrival 0, burst 7), P2 (2, 4), P3 (4, 1), P4 (5, 4). What is the average waiting time?
The Digital India programme was launched by the Government of India in the year:
questions.exp: Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015.

questions.q: Which attribute is used to merge a table cell across three rows?
questions.exp: rowspan makes a cell span the given number of rows; colspan spans columns.

questions.q: Which statement best describes an Abstract Data Type (ADT)?
options: A set of values together with operations on them, with the implementation hidden from the user
A data type whose size is fixed at compile time
A built-in type supplied by the language
A block of consecutive memory locations
questions.exp: An ADT specifies what operations are available (the interface) and hides how they are implemented.

questions.q: A cycle in the wait-for graph of a lock-based system indicates
questions.exp: A cycle means each transaction in it waits for a lock held by another in the cycle, i.e. a deadlock.

questions.q: AJAX stands for:
questions.exp: AJAX = Asynchronous JavaScript and XML.

questions.q: Which interrupt of the 8085 has the highest priority?
questions.exp: TRAP is non-maskable and has the highest priority, followed by RST 7.5, 6.5, 5.5 and INTR.

questions.q: Which method of the Thread class is used to begin execution of a new thread in Java?
questions.exp: start() creates a new call stack and invokes run() in it.

questions.q: A Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisor is one that:
options: Runs as an ordinary application on top of a host operating system
Runs directly on the host hardware without a host operating system
Is a physical network switch connecting virtual machines
Is available only as a SaaS product
questions.exp: Type 1 hypervisors such as VMware ESXi and Xen run directly on hardware.

questions.q: In Flynn's classification, a machine with one control unit that broadcasts the same instruction to many processing elements, each working on its own data, is
questions.exp: Single Instruction stream, Multiple Data streams (SIMD), e.g. array and vector processors.

questions.q: A system has 10 identical units of one resource. Allocations are P0 = 3, P1 = 2, P2 = 2 and maximum needs are P0 = 7, P1 = 4, P2 = 5. Which of the following is NOT a safe sequence?
questions.exp: Available = 10 - 7 = 3; needs: P0 4, P1 2, P2 3. P0 cannot go first (4 > 3), so any sequence starting with P0 is unsafe. P1 or P2 can start (e.g. P1, P2, P0 and P2, P0, P1 are safe).

questions.q: Which OSI layer is concerned with data encryption, compression and translation of data formats?
questions.exp: The presentation layer handles syntax, translation, encryption and compression.

questions.q: The distinguishing feature of the Spiral model compared with other process models is
options: Explicit risk analysis in every iteration
questions.exp: Each loop of the Spiral model includes risk identification and resolution, making it risk-driven.

questions.q: A relation is in BCNF if and only if, for every non-trivial functional dependency X → Y that holds in it,
options: X is a proper subset of a candidate key
Y is a subset of X
questions.exp: BCNF requires the determinant of every non-trivial FD to be a superkey.

questions.q: ZigBee is based on which IEEE standard for low-rate wireless personal area networks?
questions.exp: ZigBee builds its network and application layers on the IEEE 802.15.4 PHY and MAC.

questions.q: The BCD representation of the decimal number 47 is
questions.exp: Each decimal digit is encoded separately: 4 → 0100 and 7 → 0111.

questions.q:
What is the output of the following code?
f = lambda x, y=3: x ** y
print(f(2), f(2, 2), list(map(f, [1, 2, 3])))
questions.exp: Default y=3 gives 2**3=8; f(2,2)=4; map uses y=3 giving cubes.

questions.q: In a B-tree of order 5 (maximum 5 children per node), what is the minimum number of keys in a non-root internal node?
questions.exp: Minimum children = ceil(5/2) = 3, so minimum keys = 3 - 1 = 2.

questions.q: Which regular expression is equivalent to (a+b)*?
questions.exp: (a*b*)* can generate any sequence of a's and b's by repeating blocks, so it equals (a+b)*.

questions.q: Which transmission medium is immune to electromagnetic interference?
questions.exp: Optical fibre carries light, not electrical signals, so it is not affected by EMI.

questions.q: Which of the following is a control flag in the 8086 flag register?
questions.exp: The control flags of the 8086 are TF, IF and DF; ZF, CF and AF are status flags.

questions.q: An attacker sends a flood of TCP SYN packets and never completes the handshake, leaving the server with many half-open connections. This is a
questions.exp: A SYN flood exhausts the server's connection table with half-open connections, denying service to legitimate users.

questions.q: In the five-state process model, a running process moves to the ready state when:
options: the I/O it was waiting for completes
it is first created by the system
questions.exp: Timer interrupt at the end of the quantum preempts the running process and places it in the ready queue; I/O request leads to blocked state.

questions.q: Which sequence of Git commands correctly saves a local change and then shares it with a remote repository?
options: git commit, git add, git pull
git push, git add, git commit
git clone, git push, git commit
git add, git commit, git push
questions.exp: Changes are staged (git add), recorded in the local repository (git commit), then uploaded (git push).

questions.q: An 8-bit ADC in a microcontroller uses a 5 V reference. The number of distinct digital output codes is
questions.exp: An n-bit ADC has 2^n codes: 2^8 = 256, so each step is about 5/256 = 19.5 mV.

questions.q: Which statement about C++ destructors is correct?
options: A class can have several overloaded destructors
A destructor can take one int parameter
A destructor has no parameters and cannot be overloaded
A destructor must always be called explicitly
questions.exp: A destructor is written ~ClassName(), takes no arguments and has no return type, so only one exists per class.

questions.q: Which of the following is a recommended green computing practice?
options: Enabling sleep or power-saving mode on idle computers
Keeping all desktops switched on overnight for updates
Using animated screen savers instead of sleep mode
Throwing old monitors into ordinary household waste
questions.exp: Power management reduces energy consumption of idle systems.

questions.q: R(A, B) = {(1,x), (2,y), (3,x)}. The number of tuples in π_B(R) is
questions.exp: Projection removes duplicates; the distinct B values are x and y, so 2 tuples.

questions.q: A relation has 4 attributes and its only candidate key is a single attribute A. How many superkeys does it have?
questions.exp: Every superkey must contain A; the other 3 attributes can be included or excluded freely, giving 2³ = 8.

questions.q: In branch and bound for a minimisation problem, a live node is pruned when
options: its lower bound is less than the best cost found so far
it is a leaf node of the state space tree
its lower bound is greater than or equal to the cost of the best solution found so far
it has more than two children
questions.exp: If even the optimistic estimate cannot beat the current best, the subtree cannot contain a better solution.

questions.q: Attenuation of a signal over a long cable is overcome by using
options: twisting the wires of the cable
questions.exp: Attenuation is loss of signal strength with distance; amplifiers or repeaters regenerate it. Twisting and shielding reduce crosstalk, and CRC detects errors only.

questions.q: How many usable host addresses are available in the network 192.168.10.0/28?
questions.exp: /28 leaves 4 host bits: 2⁴ − 2 = 14 usable hosts.

questions.q: What is the number of states in the minimal DFA for the language of strings over {a,b} whose third symbol from the right end is a?
questions.exp: The DFA must remember the last 3 symbols, requiring 2^3 = 8 states, and this is minimal.

questions.q: In Java, variables declared inside an interface are implicitly:
questions.exp: Interface fields are constants: public, static and final.
Adds 1,2,4,5; 3 is skipped by continue; at i=6 continue skips, at i=7 break ends: total 12.

questions.q: How many comparators does a 4-bit flash (parallel) ADC need?
questions.exp: A flash ADC needs 2^n - 1 comparators: 2^4 - 1 = 15, and a priority encoder converts the thermometer code to binary.

questions.q: An ethical (white-hat) hacker differs from a malicious hacker mainly because the ethical hacker
options: Sells stolen data to the highest bidder
Attacks systems to promote a political cause
Tests systems with the owner's authorisation to find and report weaknesses
Writes malware to infect public computers
questions.exp: Authorisation and intent to improve security define ethical hacking.

questions.q: A weighted undirected graph has edges: A-B 4, A-C 2, B-C 1, B-D 5, C-D 8, C-E 10, D-E 2, D-F 6, E-F 3. What is the weight of its minimum spanning tree?
questions.exp: Kruskal picks B-C(1), A-C(2), D-E(2), E-F(3), skips A-B (cycle), picks B-D(5): 1+2+2+3+5 = 13.
This is the Fibonacci sequence 0,1,1,2,3,5,8,13: f(7) = 13.

questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of a RISC processor?
options: Variable-length instructions with many memory-to-memory operations
A very large number of addressing modes
questions.exp: RISC uses simple fixed-length instructions and only load/store instructions access memory.

questions.q: A time-sharing operating system achieves good response time for many users by:
options: giving each user a dedicated CPU
running one job to completion at a time
switching the CPU rapidly among users' programs using a small time slice
questions.exp: Time slicing makes each user feel they have a dedicated machine.

questions.q: Keys 10, 20, 15, 30, 40 are inserted one by one into an initially empty max-heap (stored in an array, using standard sift-up). What is the final array?
In a 4-variable K-map, a group of four adjacent 1s (a quad) eliminates how many variables?
questions.exp: A group of 2ⁿ cells eliminates n variables; a quad has n = 2.
r is a reference (alias) of x, so r++ increments x to 6.

questions.q: Which intrusion detection approach compares observed traffic with a database of known attack patterns?
questions.exp: Signature-based IDS matches events against stored patterns of known attacks; anomaly-based IDS looks for deviations from a baseline.

questions.q: According to Baumrind-type styles, which teaching style generally gives the best classroom climate?
questions.exp: Warmth with firm limits leads to cooperation and self-discipline.

questions.q: Gandhi's three H's in education stand for
questions.exp: Gandhi wanted balanced development of the intellect, emotions and skills.

questions.q: The test-retest method estimates reliability by:
options: giving two different tests to different groups
giving the same test twice to the same group and correlating the scores
checking the paper twice by one teacher
questions.exp: The correlation between two administrations shows stability.

questions.q: Vivekananda's ideal of education is
questions.exp: He wanted education that builds character and strength of mind.

questions.q: Rousseau, the author of 'Emile', is a famous representative of
questions.exp: Rousseau emphasised 'back to nature' and child-centred education.

questions.q: Instructional objectives in a lesson plan should be written in:
questions.exp: Behavioural objectives can be checked by evaluation.

questions.q: In Morris Hunt's classification, which level of teaching is the highest?
questions.exp: Memory is the lowest, understanding is the middle and reflective level (problem-centred, critical thinking) is the highest.

questions.q: According to NEP 2020, the secondary stage covers the ages of:
questions.exp: The secondary stage consists of Grades 9 to 12.

questions.q: The crisis of 'Trust versus Mistrust' occurs in
questions.exp: Consistent caregiving in the first year builds basic trust.

questions.q: Before writing a program in a class, a teacher should first ask students to:
questions.exp: Planning the logic first improves problem-solving.

questions.q: The classification of people into introverts and extroverts was given by
questions.exp: Jung classified personality as introvert or extrovert on the basis of the direction of libido.

questions.q: Which provision is most suitable for a gifted child in the regular classroom?
options: Repetition of the same easy work
questions.exp: Enrichment offers deeper, broader learning matching high ability.

questions.q: An example of hidden curriculum is:
options: students learning algebra from a textbook
students learning punctuality by watching their teacher always come on time
questions.exp: Such learning is not formally listed in any syllabus.

questions.q: Vygotsky's theory is generally known as
questions.exp: Vygotsky emphasised the role of culture and social interaction in cognitive development.

questions.q: The period of adolescence roughly covers the age of
questions.exp: Adolescence is the transition between childhood and adulthood during the teen years.

questions.q: Which of the following is an audio-visual aid?
questions.exp: A video film presents both pictures and sound.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of formative assessment?
options: A short class quiz followed by feedback
questions.exp: A short quiz with feedback helps improve learning during the course.

questions.q: The principle that development proceeds from the head towards the feet is called
questions.exp: Cephalocaudal means head-to-tail: a child gains control of the head before the trunk and legs.

questions.q: A child pours water from a short wide glass into a tall thin glass and says the amount is the same. This child has grasped
questions.exp: Conservation is the understanding that quantity remains unchanged despite changes in appearance; it appears in the concrete operational stage.

questions.q: Which teaching practice best respects individual differences?
questions.exp: Differentiated instruction adjusts content, process and product to learner needs.

questions.q: DIKSHA is:
options: a national digital platform for school education e-content
questions.exp: DIKSHA (Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing) provides e-content, QR-coded textbooks and teacher training.

questions.q: Teachers' Day in India is celebrated on:
questions.exp: It marks the birth anniversary of Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan.

questions.q: In directive counselling the main role is played by the
questions.exp: Directive counselling (Williamson) is counsellor-centred.

questions.q: What is the correct order in dealing with learning difficulties?
options: Identify the problem, diagnose the cause, apply the remedy
questions.exp: A remedy is useful only after the difficulty and its cause are known.

questions.q: Which is the correct sequence of the microteaching cycle?
questions.exp: The cycle is repeated until the skill is mastered.

questions.q: The demonstration method is most suitable when:
options: students need to practise typing speed
the class has very few students
an experiment is costly or hazardous for students to perform individually
questions.exp: The teacher performs the activity while students observe, saving cost and avoiding danger.

questions.q: Objective-type tests are called objective because:
options: scoring does not depend on the examiner's personal judgement
questions.exp: The answer key is fixed, so any scorer gives the same marks.

questions.q: The main purpose of action research in a classroom is to:
options: solve an immediate practical problem and improve practice
questions.exp: Action research is aimed at local, practical improvement.

questions.q: The RTE Act is based on which constitutional provision?
questions.exp: Article 21A, inserted by the 86th Amendment (2002), makes education a fundamental right.

questions.q: A child shares sweets with a sibling only to avoid being scolded. This reflects
options: preconventional level, obedience and punishment orientation
questions.exp: Avoiding punishment as the reason for good behaviour marks Stage 1.

questions.q: Which of the following was among the first recipients of the Bharat Ratna in 1954?
questions.exp: The 1954 awardees were C. Rajagopalachari, S. Radhakrishnan and C. V. Raman.

questions.q: The Battle of Plassey, which laid the foundation of British rule in India, was fought in
questions.exp: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 between Robert Clive and Siraj-ud-Daulah.

questions.q: Which is the highest peak lying entirely within India?
questions.exp: Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) is the highest peak in India; K2 and Everest are not wholly in India.

questions.q: The famous Nalanda Mahavihara is traditionally believed to have been founded by which Gupta ruler?
questions.exp: Nalanda was founded in the 5th century CE under Kumaragupta I; Dharmapala founded Vikramshila.

questions.q: What is the minimum age required to be elected as the President of India?
questions.exp: Article 58 requires a candidate to have completed 35 years of age.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the biodiversity hotspots found in India?
questions.exp: The Amazon basin is in South America; India has parts of Himalaya, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma and Sundaland hotspots.

questions.q:
Statement I: Carbon dioxide is the main gas responsible for enhanced global warming due to human activities.
Statement II: Burning of fossil fuels and deforestation increase atmospheric CO2.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.exp: Fossil fuel burning and deforestation raise CO2, the largest contributor to anthropogenic warming.

questions.q: Eutrophication of a lake is mainly caused by an excess of
questions.exp: Nutrient enrichment causes algal blooms; decay of algae depletes dissolved oxygen.

questions.q: The Indian Parliament enacted the Environment (Protection) Act in 1986 following which event?
questions.exp: The Bhopal gas leak (1984) of methyl isocyanate prompted the umbrella Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

questions.q: The Kyoto Protocol, adopted in 1997, mainly aims at
options: Reducing greenhouse gas emissions of industrialised countries
Controlling trade in wild fauna and flora
Banning transboundary movement of hazardous wastes
questions.exp: The Kyoto Protocol set legally binding GHG reduction targets for developed countries.

questions.q: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. What is the largest angle?
questions.exp: Sum of angles 180°; one part = 180/9 = 20°; largest = 4 x 20 = 80°.

questions.q: In a class of 50 students, 30 like tea, 25 like coffee and 10 like both. How many like neither?
questions.exp: Students liking at least one = 30 + 25 - 10 = 45; neither = 50 - 45 = 5.

questions.q: Which activity is most suitable for introducing the idea of a fraction as part of a whole to Class VI learners?
options: Memorising rules for adding fractions with unlike denominators
Solving a long list of fraction problems from the textbook
Dictating the definition of a fraction to be copied down
Folding paper strips or circles into equal parts and shading some of them
questions.exp: Concrete, hands-on activities such as paper folding build conceptual understanding before symbolic rules.

questions.q: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 11?
questions.exp: For 2728: (2 + 2) - (7 + 8) = -11, a multiple of 11 (2728 = 11 x 248). The others give differences -7, -2 and -3.

questions.q: What is the compound interest on Rs 8000 for 2 years at 10% per annum compounded annually?
What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 4:30?
questions.exp: Hour hand = 4×30 + 15 = 135°; minute hand = 180°; difference = 45°.

questions.q: Five persons P, Q, R, S, T sit in a row facing north. T is at the extreme left end and P is at the extreme right end. Q sits immediately to the left of R, and S sits to the left of Q. Who sits in the middle?
questions.exp: T is 1st and P is 5th. S, Q, R must fill places 2, 3, 4 in that order (S left of Q, Q immediately left of R). So Q is in the middle.

questions.q: If + means ×, − means ÷, × means + and ÷ means −, then the value of 12 + 3 − 4 × 5 ÷ 2 is:
In a group of 60 people, 35 like tea, 28 like coffee and 10 like neither. How many like both tea and coffee?
questions.exp: People liking at least one = 60 − 10 = 50. Both = 35 + 28 − 50 = 13.

questions.q:
Statement: All successful teachers are punctual. Ravi is a successful teacher.
Conclusions: I. Ravi is punctual. II. All punctual persons are teachers.
questions.exp: Ravi belongs to the class of successful teachers, all of whom are punctual, so I follows. The converse in II is not given.
